_doc: Reproduction record of the baseline arms (src/eval/baselines/record.py reads and writes it).
An arm may run only the (dataset, protocol) pairs listed in its own `targets` until its status is `verified`.
`published` is the number as printed in the source (a string, so the printed digits are kept);
`scale` converts our value to the printed unit (100 for a percentage). `gate: false` targets are
recorded but cannot verify an arm; `why_not_gating` says what is missing. `dataset: null` = not
runnable here. `reference_only` rows come from another paper: they authorise nothing.
Transcribed from the arXiv HTML renderings fetched 2026-10-03; nothing is quoted from memory.

vda.name: Video Depth Anything (VDA-L)
vda.settings: benchmark/infer/infer.py: input_size 518 (short side, reduced when aspect > 1.78), fp32, 32-frame windows. Data settings found by running VDA's own unmodified scripts on variants of the tree (2026-10-04, jobs 6327481, 6327549, 6327659, 6327762): Bonn = all 26 sequences (`bonn_all`, `bonn_all_500`), which is what its extractor takes; Sintel = colour files with R and B swapped on disk (`sintel_bgr`), which is what its extractor writes; ScanNet TAE over all 100 scenes, because its 20 are the first 20 of an unsorted glob and cannot be recovered.
vda.status_note: Verified 2026-10-08 at code 210603e+1fb2f7a0 (jobs 6351249, 6353003, 6353004): 15 of 15 gating targets, all measured by that one code state. First verified 2026-10-05 (jobs 6329345, 6329347) under the legacy '+dirty' code string, which identified no code state. What it took, each measured with VDA's own unmodified scripts first: Bonn over all 26 sequences (bonn_all, bonn_all_500; the 5 DepthCrafter sequences give 0.0592 / 0.0821 instead of 0.053 / 0.071); Sintel on R/B-swapped colour files, as its extractor writes them (sintel_bgr 0.2981; true colours 0.3010; paper 0.295); ScanNet TAE over all 100 scenes (0.5659; paper 0.570 on an unrecoverable 20 -- the first 20 of an unsorted glob; a 20-scene mean has std 0.038). Ruled out along the way: Sintel depth encoding and depth cap; colour order for Bonn and TAE; TAE colour resolution (1296x968: 0.6020); Bonn timestamp pairing (other side of the paper: 0.0506 / 0.0681 on 5 sequences).

vda_metric.name: Metric Video Depth Anything (Metric-VDA-L)
vda_metric.paper: none: the metric models postdate arXiv:2501.12375; the only published numbers are the upstream README release notes (2025-08-28)
vda_metric.settings: as vda, with metric=True (no window alignment), except that the metric model runs WITHOUT infer_video_depth's aspect shrink: frames wider than 16:9 get the input_size that the shrink maps back to 518 (arms.unshrunk_input_size; KITTI 374x1242 -> 957), and its DINOv2 attention runs through torch scaled_dot_product_attention so the unshrunk frames fit in memory (same math; upstream's MemEffAttention falls back to plain attention without xFormers). The README does not state split, frame cap or alignment; ASSUMED: delta1 without alignment on the 500-frame split, TAE as eval_tae.sh.
vda_metric.status_note: Recorded CLOSE by user decision (2026-10-13): compared under --allow-close with the gap reported. Re-measured 2026-10-13 at code 7d171b6+88100c79 (job 6385433): KITTI-500 delta1 0.9063 within tolerance (README 0.910); ScanNet TAE 1.0599, CLOSE, not passed (README 1.09, +-0.0218), so the computed status stays failed. ScanNet TAE: CLOSE, not passed (user decision 2026-10-12). Three-way on the same fp32 predictions of the unshrunk arm (job 6383596): ours 1.0599 (100 scenes) / 1.0798 (first 20 of our manifest order); VDA's own eval_tae.py, unmodified, on 1/depth 1.0599 / 1.0797 (matches ours to 1e-4); on raw metric depth 1.2720 / 1.3359 (so the README did not feed depth unconverted). README 1.09, tolerance +-0.0218. eval_tae.sh scores 20 scenes in an unrecoverable glob order; resampling our per-scene values (0.63-2.20), a 20-scene mean spans 0.963-1.166 (5-95%), so the 2.6% gap is inside that draw noise but cannot be closed. Precision ruled out (fp16 1.0604, fp32 1.0599, job 6378672). KITTI-500 delta1 through the staged arm: 0.9063 fp32 / 0.9063 fp16 (README 0.910, within tolerance; job 6378672). 2026-10-11/12: KITTI cause found. The aspect shrink in infer_video_depth (a memory workaround, 'due to memory limitation') sets KITTI's short side to 280; unshrunk at 518 the scale is right: KITTI-500 raw metric delta1 0.9074 / AbsRel 0.1050 / median gt/pred 1.005 vs shrunk 0.3424 / 0.3466 / 0.764 (fp16, H100, probe job 6373139, eval_jd/baselines/mvda_probe/). R/B-swapped input changes nothing (0.3435 vs 0.3427, job 6372713). The arm now runs unshrunk. Earlier notes: Not reproduced; README protocol unrecoverable. What was established (jobs 6329352, 6329880, 6333457; upstream git history): the metric model's own inference code at the time of the README table (metric_depth/video_depth.py, 2025-08-29) is the shared code of today, aspect shrink included, and the L checkpoint on HF (2025-04-22) predates the table, so code and weights are theirs. Raw metric delta1 is 0.344-0.366 on KITTI (full frame; the aspect shrink to a 280 px short side changes the scale: median gt/pred 0.77; a 16:9 centre crop gives 0.953) and 0.5835 on our NYUv2 stills (480x640, no shrink; AbsRel 0.25, a scale error on indoor data). With a per-video scale alignment: KITTI-500 0.9218 (scale-only LSQ) / 0.9318 (median), NYUv2 0.9448 / 0.9541 -- the README's 0.910 / 0.908 sit in that range but match no single alignment, and the README's NYU is its 8-scene 500-frame video split, not built here. Undoing the shrink at full width runs out of memory on an 80 GB H100. CONSEQUENCE: this arm's absolute scale depends on input resolution and camera, so in our `metric` table it is only meaningful with the input convention stated, and not on frames wider than 16:9 uncropped.

dav.name: Depth Any Video
dav.settings: Sec. 4.2: 3 denoising steps, ensemble size 20 'following Ke et al. (2024)', and evaluation 'following prior methods (Ke et al., 2024; Fu et al., 2024)', i.e. Marigold's. The arm runs the released pipeline 20 times (seeds 0-19) and averages the disparities (no ensembling code is released). All three gating datasets use Marigold's own evaluation data, split lists and least_square_disparity protocol (src/eval/marigold_paper.py, third_party/marigold_eval): NYUv2 = the 654 test frames of nyu_labeled_extracted, raw depth, Eigen crop [45:471, 41:601], 1e-3 < GT < 10, run at 480x640; KITTI Eigen 652 kb-cropped to 352x1216 and run at that size (run_infer's --max_resolution = its long side), 1e-5 < GT < 80, Eigen mask; ScanNet = the 800-frame sample Marigold ships, 1e-3 < GT < 10.
dav.status_note: Verified 2026-10-14 (job 6393331, started 2026-10-13 21:06): all six Table 2 targets on Marigold's data and protocol, 20-seed ensemble: NYUv2 5.03 / 96.94 (paper 5.1 / 97.0), KITTI 7.27 / 95.05 (7.3 / 95.1), ScanNet 5.21 / 96.62 (5.3 / 96.6). The recorded code string abeb6d4+e3e51181 was taken when the job ENDED (the start-of-run fingerprint fix came later), so it also covers edits made while it ran: the gate consolidation, the status CLI, compare_table, tae_ours' float32 origin and da3_metric's per-frame focal. None is on DAV's scoring path (DAVArm.predict, run_marigold, marigold_paper.py were unchanged from 21:06). 2026-10-13 (code review): the NYUv2 targets moved from our nyuv2_raw tree scored with VDA's alignment to Marigold's own NYU data and protocol, so all of DAV's gating targets share the one protocol the settings name (VDA's fit keeps pixels with zero predicted disparity, Marigold's excludes them). Pending a reproduce run of all six targets at one code state. 2026-10-13: KITTI and ScanNet made gating (user decision), on Marigold's own data and protocol; the status is pending until one reproduce run at one code state measures all six targets. Before that, NYUv2 alone was verified (job 6385432). SUPERSEDED HISTORY (before the move to Marigold's NYU data and protocol; the nyuv2_raw tree named below was removed, and its NYU numbers used VDA's alignment, so they are not comparable with the next run): Verified 2026-10-13 at code 7d171b6+88100c79 (job 6385432): NYUv2 AbsRel 5.03 / delta1 96.95 (paper 5.1 / 97.0) with the 20-seed ensemble on raw GT. Corroborated 2026-10-13 on two non-gating Table 2 rows, outside this pipeline (probe scripts in eval_jd/baselines/parity2/scripts/, Marigold's own evaluation data and protocol, 20-seed mean): KITTI Eigen 652 (kb crop, Eigen mask, 1e-5..80 m) 7.27 / 95.05 vs 7.3 / 95.1 (job 6389357); ScanNet, Marigold's 800-frame sample, 5.21 / 96.62 vs 5.3 / 96.6 (job 6389439). Our nyuv2_raw tree matches Marigold's NYU test data (identical RGB, depth within its 1 mm storage step). 2026-10-13, lineage check: the gap was the GT. Our earlier `nyuv2_full` tree holds the FILLED depth (`depths`); Marigold, whose evaluation DAV follows, scores against the raw depth. On the same saved predictions (jobs 6329351, 6384434; scored through score_main): raw GT seed 0 5.38 / 96.66, mean of 10 seeds 5.03 / 96.98, mean of 20 seeds 5.03 / 96.95; filled GT seed 0 6.64 / 94.65 (the old record), mean of 20 6.20 / 95.09. Marigold's own ensemble_depth on 20 seeds vs the mean, first 200 images (job 6384957, did not finish the set): 5.19 / 96.69 vs 5.16 / 96.74. Targets moved to nyuv2_raw and the arm to the 20-seed mean. Earlier notes: Not reproducible from the release: NYUv2 6.64 / 94.65 vs 5.1 / 97.0 (full 480x640 frame, Eigen crop, per-image scale+shift in disparity). One variable at a time (jobs 6329351, 6329855; offline analysis of 10 saved seeds per image): ensembling 10 seeds 6.18 / 95.12 (mean) and saturating, so the paper's ensemble of 20 does not close it; fitting in depth space as Marigold does 13.2 / 84.0; R/B-swapped input 6.81; input upscaled to 768x1024 7.41; 1 step 6.75; 10 steps 6.93. No evaluation or data code is released; the remaining candidates (the released checkpoint differing from the paper's, an unreleased ensembling/alignment procedure) cannot be tested.

ovda.name: Online Video Depth Anything (oVDA-small, context 16)
ovda.settings: The authors' own evaluation (third_party/ovda/evaluation, sent by the first author 2026-10-08), run through src/eval/ovda_paper.py: Sintel final pass with .dpt GT (23 sequences, 1064 frames); Bonn all 26 sequences, RGB/depth paired by timestamp (< 20 ms, greedy one-to-one; 29,064 pairs); KITTI the 138 data_depth_annotated/train drives, image_03 and image_02 as separate sequences (276 sequences, 85,898 frames), no crop. Only paired frames are fed; infer_video_depth(input_size=518) (fp32 here, fp16 in the paper). Their protocol: per-sequence fit of the inverse-depth prediction to 1/GT on frame 0 (ovda_first) or all frames (ovda_all), GT valid 0 < GT < limit (Sintel 10000, KITTI 255.9, Bonn 100 m) and unclipped in the fit, prediction clipped to [0, 80] m, scoring on GT < 80 m from frame 1, pixel-weighted over the dataset, delta1 <= 1.25.
ovda.status_note: Retargeted 2026-10-08 to the authors' reference evaluation. Check before the retarget: their protocol.py on our saved Sintel final-pass predictions (job 6321823) gives first-frame 0.3799 / 0.5477 and global 0.2941 / 0.6035 against the paper's 0.380 / 0.548 and 0.294 / 0.604, so our inference was right and every earlier gap was scoring and data (the 'clip GT at 80 m' match of 2026-10-04 on the clean pass was two wrong settings cancelling). Verified 2026-10-08 at code 210603e+1fb2f7a0 (jobs 6352383 KITTI, 6353005 Sintel + Bonn): 12 of 12 gating targets. The four Table 8 '500' targets are non-gating and not run.

promptda.name: Prompt Depth Anything (ViT-L)
promptda.settings: Sec. 4.1: ARKitScenes depth-upsampling protocol (ARKitScenes paper), Validation fold (5,599 images): 192x256 ARKit depth as the prompt, laser-scan highres depth as GT, evaluated at 384x512 / 768x1024 / 1440x1920. No evaluation code is released; ASSUMED from apple/ARKitScenes depth_upsampling/dataset.py: GT nearest-resized to the evaluated size, frames rotated upright by sky_direction, L1 and RMSE in metres over GT > 0, mean over images. Inference is upstream's default (io_wrapper.load_image: long side capped at 1008, i.e. 756x1008), ONE prediction per frame, bilinearly resized to each evaluated size.
promptda.status_note: Recorded CLOSE by user decision (2026-10-13): compared under --allow-close with the gap reported. 2026-10-13, lineage check: Sec. 4.1 follows the ARKitScenes paper's suggested protocol, and the MSPF row is taken from it (App. C.4). Apple's depth_upsampling code (logs/eval.py, train.py validation transforms): per-image L1 / RMSE, GT nearest-resized, mean over images, as ours; it also masks GT > 0.01 m (ours GT > 0; tested below, no change) and applies ModCrop(32) (a no-op at 384x512, 768x1024, 1440x1920). The one upstream code change since the paper is 29ba2fa (2025-01-17, 'Fix the image normalization bug'): the first public code (e76db21) fed DINOv2 unnormalised images; the weights (2024-12-16) predate both. Full fold (job 6384439): normalised (the arm) 384 0.0132 / 0.0317, 768 0.0131 / 0.0312, 1440 0.0131 / 0.0311; unnormalised 0.0139 / 0.0332, 0.0138 / 0.0327, 0.0137 / 0.0325. The paper (0.0135 / 0.0326, 0.0132 / 0.0315, 0.0138 / 0.0316) sits between the two and matches neither (normalised 3 of 6 within tolerance, unnormalised 2 of 6); the arm keeps the current, normalised code. CLOSE, not passed: all six within 5.3% of the paper, three within tolerance. Within 5.1% on all six targets, three within tolerance (job 6322208): 384x512 0.0132 / 0.0317 vs 0.0135 / 0.0326; 768x1024 0.0131 / 0.0312 vs 0.0132 / 0.0315; 1440x1920 0.0131 / 0.0311 vs 0.0138 / 0.0316. One variable at a time on the first 20 videos (jobs 6329348, 6329881; change in L1 / RMSE vs the one-inference base): inference at each column's size +21% / +12% at 384 and +19% / +11% at 1440 (ruled out; +1.2% / +2.6% at 768); no upright rotation +21% / +10% (ruled out); R/B-swapped input +2.1% / +2.0% in every column; ARKit prompt resized to 180x240 at 1440, as Apple's x8 loader does, +2.1% / +0.5%; prediction resized nearest +1.4% / +4.2% at 384, cubic +0.1% / +1.0%; validity gt > 0.01 m: no change. The paper differs from our base by +2.3% / +2.8% (384), +0.8% / +1.0% (768), +5.3% / +1.6% (1440): no single variable gives that pattern, and none was adopted. No evaluation code is released.

runs.note: This run resized the RGB to each evaluated size before inference (378x504 for the 384x512 column). 768x1024 reproduced (0.0133 / 0.0319 vs 0.0132 / 0.0315); 384x512 did not (0.0161 / 0.0359 vs 0.0135 / 0.0326). da3_metric.name: Depth Anything 3, monocular metric (DA3METRIC-LARGE)
da3_metric.settings: The paper (Sec. 7.4, Table 11) names no evaluation protocol and the repository ships no metric-depth evaluation; the protocol is built from what Sec. 4.4 states about the metric model: base resolution 504, aspect ratios 1:1 to 1:2. Frames wider than 1:2 are centre-cropped to 1:2 with their GT (KITTI 375x1242 -> 375x750; NYUv2 4:3 untouched), then DA3's API with the short side at 504 (process_res=504, lower_bound_resize, sky post-process on), metric depth = output * mean(fx, fy) / 300 at the processed resolution (README). Scored with Depth Anything V2's metric_depth eval loop (third_party/depth_anything_v2_metric; src/eval/da_metric_paper.py): prediction bilinear (align_corners) to GT, valid 0.001 <= GT <= 80 m, no clip, per-image eval_depth, mean over images. NYUv2: the 654 official test frames of nyu_depth_v2_labeled.mat, lossless RGB, rawDepths GT. KITTI: DA2's 652-frame Eigen list with annotated GT, image_02 PNG, focal from P_rect_02 per date.
da3_metric.status_note: Verified 2026-10-11 at code 5db3f2d+81ad99cc (job 6372550): 4 of 4 gating targets, NYUv2 0.0701 / 0.9671 and KITTI 0.0866 / 0.9499, matching the probe to 1e-4. ETH3D, SUN-RGBD and DIODE are non-gating and not run. Protocol found by a probe outside this pipeline (2026-10-10/11, 25 GPU jobs 6366320-6372440, scripts and results in eval_jd/baselines/da3_probe/), one variable at a time. Probe values for this protocol: NYUv2 0.0700 / 0.9671 (lossless frames; 0.0709 / 0.9648 with the BTS JPEG frames), KITTI 0.0866 / 0.9499 (job 6372440); also within tolerance with a 1:1.8 crop (0.0875 / 0.9495) and a 20 m cap (0.0864 / 0.9595). The decisive step was the 1:2 crop: without it, short side 504 gives KITTI 0.0833 / 0.9509, and DA3's default resize (long side 504) 0.0969 / 0.9164 with an 80 m cap or 0.0857 / 0.9502 with DA2's default 20 m cap, which in turn misses NYUv2 (0.0726). Fitting KITTI into 504x1008 by padding (Metric3D style) gives 0.0668, so the paper cropped. Ruled out (change < 0.001 or away from the paper): fp16 / bf16 / fp32 and V100S / A40 / H100 (identical to 1e-4), the first public code (6c58ec9, 2025-11-14; within 5e-4), crop vs resize to a multiple of 14, prediction clipping, Eigen and Garg crops, flip TTA, raw LiDAR GT (0.108), pixel-pooled metrics, scoring at the network resolution, KITTI val_selection_cropped, sky post-process, one focal for every KITTI date. Also found: KITTI AbsRel depends on the parity of the processed height in patches (odd 0.090-0.097, even 0.081-0.088) and on input chroma (4:2:0 subsampling 0.0729 vs PNG 0.0833; JPEG 4:4:4 = PNG). arXiv v1 is the only version; the HF weights have one upload (2025-11-13).
